items.item_text: 01. Which statement below best describes the highest level of education you have completed? Options: Some High School | High school graduate, diploma or the equivalent (GED) | Some college (less than 60 units) | Associate degree or at least 60 semester units | Bachelor's degree | Master's degree | Professional degree | Doctorate degree
02. Do you have an Associates Degree or higher in counseling, career education, behavioral science, human services, or a closely related field. ? Options: Yes | No

03. How many years of increasingly responsible clerical or administrative support experience do you have involving college and career development, scholarship or financial aid programs, or other post-secondary and career resources? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year of experience | 1 year but less than 2 years of experience | 2 years but less than 3 years experience | 3 years but less than 4 years experience | 4 years or more

04. Please describe your clerical or administrative support experience involving college and career development, scholarship or financial aid programs, or other post-secondary and career resources. Include the following information for each relevant position held: (a) Job Title: (b) Organization/Agency Name: (c) Key Relevant Duties: (d) Employment Period: (From MM/YYYY to MM/YYYY) If you have no relevant experience in this area, enter "N/A."

Maintains resources and coordinates events for the College and Career Center, working with post-secondary institutions and District staff to broaden student access to college and career opportunities.
Assists students in developing career goals by administering, scoring, and interpreting career interest assessments.
Delivers classroom presentations and conducts College and Career Center orientations covering various higher education and career pathways.

Coordinates and collaborates with counselors and other district staff to communicate college application, entrance exam, transcript, and financial aid requirements, scholarships and deadlines to students.
Coordinates Center events, including presentations from career speakers, college and military representatives; and career visitations from local businesses and industry.

Maintains a variety of confidential and non-confidential manual and electronic lists and records (e.g. inventory of college catalogues, application and web site locations, etc.) for the purpose of ensuring the availability of material for internal use and distribution as required.
Participates in conferences, workshops, and training to stay current on financial aid options and college entry criteria.
Performs related duties as assigned.
Career guidance and student advisement techniques
Coordinate the resources, activities, and events of a college and career center at an assigned site
Post-secondary education, vocational training, and military career opportunities
Administer, score, and interpret career interest assessments and surveys
Career interest survey administration, scoring, and interpretation methodS
Provide classroom presentations and center orientations to students and families
Modern office practices, procedures, and software, including student information systems, college admissions and financial aid application systems
Research and compile college, career, scholarship, and financial aid information into usable resources
Data collection and report preparation methods
Identify student interests and goals, and guide students in exploring career and college options
Recruitment and retention programs and techniques
Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others.
Effective written and verbal communication techniques
Prepare and maintain accurate records, reports, databases, and files
College admissions guidelines, entrance examination requirements, and application procedures
Work independently with minimal direction.
Financial aid, scholarship, and grant resources and application processes
Model communications and interactions that respect and include individuals of all languages, abilities, religions, and cultures.
Federal and state laws and District policies governing the confidentiality of student records
Interpersonal skills using tact, patience and courtesy
Identify student interests, skills, and goals, and guide students in exploring appropriate options
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing.
Operate standard office equipment
